rationale: The candidate is a clean, manifold split-wing mass, but it fails the program contract for neighborhood living. In the four views it reads mostly as two rectangular solids separated by a narrow seam, with the ground response to the verified access edge remaining weak and semantically vague. The mass is coherent in plan and section enough to avoid collision or repair problems, but it does not yet produce a convincing active threshold, public void, or clear ground-level communal figure. The silhouette is orderly, but it is boxy and under-articulated for the brief; it resembles a generic dual-block extrusion more than a compact capacity-aware street building. The best reference lesson is not the tall towers, but the counterfactual 8 House principle: a continuous sectional/massing rule that creates a legible public space and preserves one dominant gesture. As shown, the proposal needs either a carved court/open side or a stronger ground spine/entry seam aligned to access.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered upper massing can stay coherent when it remains one dominant body with a clear datum.
